findings_assessed.observation: Firebase API key and Google Maps API key exposed in __NUXT__ config
findings_assessed.reason: Firebase web API keys are designed to be public client-side identifiers. Security relies on Firestore/RTDB rules and App Check. No evidence of misconfigured security rules or data access without auth. Google Maps API key is similarly client-side by design.

findings_assessed.observation: Next.js app with buildId ai1p012afoT-TnRBe5nvA, empty pageProps
findings_assessed.reason: No sensitive data in __NEXT_DATA__. Data endpoints return 404. No IDOR or info disclosure vectors found via passive probing.

findings_assessed.observation: Healthera Core platform, /api/v1 and /api/v2 return empty {"data":[]}
findings_assessed.reason: API requires authentication. Empty responses are expected for unauthenticated requests. No swagger/openapi/docs exposed.
Weak CSP alone is not a reportable vulnerability without a demonstrated XSS or injection vector. Site appears to be a simple marketing landing page with no user input or dynamic content processing.

exhausted_vectors: Swagger/OpenAPI enumeration on api.superdrug.com and api.savers.co.uk
GraphQL endpoint discovery on app.pharmacy and appt.healthclinics
Next.js data endpoint abuse on appt.healthclinics
robots.txt and sitemap.xml on all responsive targets
Security headers analysis on all Tier 1 and Tier 4 targets
recommendation: No high-confidence actionable vulnerability identified through passive reconnaissance. Akamai WAF blocks most automated probing on Tier 1 assets. Recommend pivoting to next program. Mobile app testing (iOS/Android) would require device-level analysis not feasible in current headless environment.
